assertions.name: mirror_split_proportional_to_canonical_coulomb_all_A
assertions.source: split_AME/ΔE_C(canonical Z(Z−1), r₀=1.2) = 0.987 ± 0.069 (7% spread) across 8 mirror pairs A=3–39 ⇒ the split is proportional to Coulomb ⇒ the strong kernel must be charge-symmetric. The spread is a monotone TREND, not constant scatter (Pearson r = 0.830); the proportionality conclusion is unaffected.

assertions.name: mirror_ratio_trends_monotonically_with_A
assertions.source: Pearson r = 0.830 between split/ΔE_C and A over the 8 pairs; t = 3.65 on 6 dof exceeds the 2.447 two-sided p=0.05 critical value, and a straight line has rms 0.0387 against the mean's 0.0694. Recorded so 'ratio_mean' is not consumed as if it applied at every A — at A=3 the ratio is 0.901.

description: The mirror binding split is Coulomb across the isobaric chain ³H/³He…³⁹K/³⁹Ca: using the repo's canonical uniform-sphere Coulomb (Z(Z−1) self-energy, r₀=1.2 fm, coulomb_energy.mirror_displacement_mev — NO free parameter), the ratio split_AME/ΔE_C = 0.99 ± 0.07 across A=3–39 (the ~0.8 factor is the known uniform-sphere over-estimate). ⇒ the split is proportional to Coulomb, so any QOU strong kernel must be charge-symmetric (Coulomb separate); the #2089 kernel's 2.27 MeV A=3 strong split (#3564) is 3× the whole observed split, systematically. Scope-(a), no wiring. ⚠ THE RATIO IS NOT CONSTANT (corrected 2026-08-25): this field said '≈constant across A=3–39'. It rises monotonically — Pearson r = 0.830, t = 3.65 on 6 dof (p < 0.05), and a line beats the mean by 44% in rms. The proportionality finding and the charge-symmetry consequence are unaffected; only the 'constant' characterisation was wrong. Consumers must say WHICH A: the A=3 (³H/³He) ratio is 0.901, not the chain mean 0.99.

ratio_trend_in_A.note: The ratio is NOT constant in A; it rises monotonically. A line describes the eight points better than their mean. Quote the A you need, not ratio_mean.
